714128.t: Inherited from Proto-Indo-European *yóh₁r̥ (“year, season”). Cognate with English year.

714125.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *ōyyón, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), argued to have been a derivative of *h₂éwis (“bird”), whence also ἀετός (āetós, “eagle”) and οἰωνός (oiōnós, “bird of prey”).

714114.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃émōs. Cognates include Sanskrit अंस॑ (áṃsa), Latin umerus, Old Armenian ուս (us), and Gothic 𐌰𐌼𐍃 (ams).

714170.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰel-, cognate with Old Armenian աւելի (aweli). Cf. ὀφείλω (opheílō).

714100.t: Possible Greek relations, even if ruled out by Beekes as highly unlikely, are the verbal present form ἔθει (éthei), the participle ἔθων (éthōn, “damaging, plaguing; pushing, tossing (?)”) and the nouns ἔθρις (éthris, “castrated ram”), ἔθειρα (étheira,…

714176.t: Unknown; the traditional connection with Sanskrit व्याघ्र (vyāghrá, “tiger”) (based on a shared semantic connection of warm color) is morphologically unconvincing.

714142.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃rewH- (“to howl, roar”), albeit with initial long ὠ- (ō-) unexplained. Cognate with Latin rūmor, Latin rāvis, Latvian rûkt, Lithuanian rū́kti, and Sanskrit रव॑ (ráva).

714158.t: From ὡς (hōs) + αὔτως (aútōs), originally written separately in Homer.
